title: Missä: answering with -ssa and -ssä
focus: Missä asks where someone or something is. Missä sinä olet? — Olen koulussa.

exercises.prompt: Choose the question meaning “Where are you?”  Address one person (sinä).
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. The inessive is the in-place form, answering where. Missä asks where someone or something is. For the inside-location pattern, put -ssa or -ssä on the taught noun stem. There is no movement into or out of the place. The complete question means “Where are you”.

parts.role: question asking where someone or something is
parts.formation: Missä is the inessive question form: it asks for the location, not a source or destination.

parts.role: subject (who or what this sentence is about)
parts.formation: Sinä addresses one person informally.

exercises.prompt: Answer “Missä hän on?”: choose “She is in the cafe.”
exercises.explanation: Singular refers to one person or one thing in these patterns. Answer with the location: koulussa (“at school”) or talossa (“in the house”). A full reply includes the appropriate verb, such as Olen koulussa (“I am at school”). A short reply Koulussa gives the same requested location. The forms of olla (“be”) are provided. The complete reply means “She is in the cafe”.
